name: Requirements Traceability Matrix
purpose: Tracks the attributes of each requirement through the project life cycle, using the requirements documentation and showing how each requirement is addressed elsewhere in the project: traced to the business objective, the WBS deliverable, the metric that measures it and the technique that validates it. A second page, the inter-requirements traceability matrix, traces the relationship between two categories of requirements (the book's sample pairs business requirements with technical requirements).

citation: Book of Forms form 2.7, PDF pages 51 to 53 (printed pages 40 to 42); blank forms PDF pages 54 to 55 (printed pages 43 to 44)
notes: The book gives no adaptive-specific text for this form; the Alignment list names a release and iteration plan (PDF page 52, printed page 41). Element order follows Table 2.6 then Table 2.7 (PDF page 53, printed page 42). Table 2.6 lists Category before Priority, but the blank form prints Priority before Category; the printed order wins on the form. On the second page ID, Priority and Source each print twice, once per requirement type, so printed_label repeats. Alternative uses the book gives for the inter-requirements matrix (PDF page 51, printed page 40): business objectives and technical requirements, functional and technical requirements, requirements and verification method, technical requirements and WBS deliverables.
